title: Armin Ronacher Leaning In To Find Out - PyAI Conf 2026
summary: Armin Ronacher argues coding agents work best on what RL session data over-represents (files, shell, common languages, SQL) and fail on external state changes, GUIs and rare tools.

assertions.quote: tool using code loops are very measurable

verdicts.note: Consistent with labs training on verifiable coding tasks, but training data composition is not public so the mechanism is inferred.

assertions.quote: anything working with something that's sort of very very common works really well
Lisp for instance, and I discovered it just doesn't really work
the thing is incredibly terrible at using UV. It will keep going back to not using UV.
because it is basically just pulling proprietary tools into the context all the time it's very hard for model to reason
it has only four tools it's the most minimal set of coding agent you can use and it still works
external state changes break this experience

verdicts.note: Agents only see state the harness reports, and false verification claims are widely observed, though harnesses increasingly detect external file changes.

assertions.quote: it just claimed that it validated it, but it didn't in fact do that
they still suck at clicking stuff in the UI even with the multimodal models
you're actually surprisingly context efficient if the data actually doesn't have to travel through the context
